sections.theory:
Administration of the sultanate

(A) Central government:

In the era of the Banu Abbas's government too the administration of the sultanate was run in approximately the same way as it was in the era of the Banu Umayyah. Only the posts of vizierate and hajib were established and some other departments were added.

1. The position of the caliph:

The caliphs of the Banu Abbas, along with being heads of government, also regarded themselves as religious leaders. In their era too, like the Banu Umayyah, a Majlis-e-Shura did not exist. The position of the caliph was that of an absolute ruler. No restriction of any kind applied to him. The caliph was also the commander-in-chief of the armies.

2. Vizierate:

The Abbasid caliphs for their own ease established the regular post of the vizierate. The post of vizierate existed in the governments of the Iranians. Viziers were of two kinds.

(a) Wazir-e-Tafwid or Madar al-Maham:

The Wazir-e-Tafwid had unlimited powers. In the government his was the second position after the caliph. He was also called Amir al-Umara'. He could use the caliph's powers too. The caliph was only given information. In many matters the caliph was even ignored. He did not need to take the caliph's prior permission. In the last era of the Abbasids the caliphs had become helpless. Power was in the hands of the viziers.

sections.title: سبق 25 — متن (117)

paras.text: These viziers had very few powers. Viziers of this kind did the work of liaison between the caliph and the public. Their work was to have the orders of the caliph and the chief vizier implemented. Their own will had no say in any matter. It was the duty of these viziers to keep themselves informed at all times of provincial affairs and local conditions.
